title: You're Taller in the Morning #science #body
description:
You're taller in the morning. Between the bones of your spine are soft discs, full of water. Standing and sitting all day squeezes water out of them, and you lose about 1 % of your height, a centimetre or two, by evening. Lying down at night, the discs soak it back up. In orbit, without gravity pressing down, astronauts' spines stretch even more, up to about 3 %.

More about your body: Why do your fingers wrinkle in water? https://youtu.be/dTu9m6gXCck

Sources
- Reilly, T., Tyrrell, A. & Troup, J. D. G. (1984), Circadian variation in human stature, Chronobiology International 1: 121–126
- Tyrrell, A. R., Reilly, T. & Troup, J. D. G. (1985), Circadian variation in stature and the effects of spinal loading, Spine 10: 161–164
- NASA: astronauts' height increases up to 3 % in microgravity (nasa.gov)
- The height gap in the animation is exaggerated

Have you ever measured yourself morning and night?

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every claim is checked against the sources above.
